Bilateral trade between Nigeria and Thailand rose by 104.73 per cent to approximately $1.88bn in the first nine months of 2026, the Thai Ambassador to Nigeria, Thirapath Mongkolnavin, has said. Mongkolnavin disclosed this at a reception held Wednesday night, in Abuja to mark the birthday anniversary of the late Thai King Bhumibol Adulyadej the Great, Thailand’s National Day and Father’s Day. The envoy said the significant increase in trade reflected growing economic ties between both countries, adding that Thailand was committed to expanding economic and development cooperation with Nigeria and other African countries. He said, “In the economic sphere, our bilateral trade reached approximately USD 1.88 billion during the first nine months of this year, representing a remarkable 104.73 per cent increase year-on-year. “Through the Thailand–Africa Initiative, Thailand remains committed to expanding economic and development cooperation with Nigeria and other African partners.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The ambassador said the two countries were preparing to mark 65 years of diplomatic relations next year, noting that recent high-level engagements had opened new opportunities for practical cooperation. He cited the visit of Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs to Nigeria, as well as the first Bilateral Consultations between both countries held in August, as significant milestones in strengthening their partnership. Mongkolnavin also identified human resource development as another key area of bilateral cooperation, saying Thailand had continued to provide training opportunities and scholarships to Nigerians through its Thailand International Cooperation Agency. According to him, the opportunities are offered under the Annual International Training Course and the Thailand International Postgraduate Programme. “We hope these programmes will continue to strengthen professional capacities, foster knowledge exchange and build lasting connections between our peoples,” he said. On regional cooperation, the envoy expressed optimism about stronger relations between the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and the Economic Community of West African States. He noted that Nigeria played an important role in ECOWAS, while Thailand was a member of ASEAN, adding that he hoped to use his position as the first Thai Ambassador to ECOWAS to promote closer engagement between the two regional blocs. “I look forward, in my capacity as the first Thai Ambassador to ECOWAS, to help fostering closer dialogue between ASEAN and ECOWAS, mutual understanding and practical cooperation for the benefit of both regions,” he said. The ambassador also paid tribute to the late King Bhumibol Adulyadej, popularly known as King Rama IX, who devoted seven decades to improving the welfare of the Thai people. He said the late monarch’s visionary leadership and Sufficiency Economy Philosophy continued to inspire Thailand’s development. He also honoured the late Queen Sirikit, the Queen Mother, for her contributions to preserving Thai arts, traditional craftsmanship and cultural identity, particularly through the promotion of Chud Thai, the country’s national dress. The reception featured Thai cuisine prepared by chefs from the ambassador’s residence and Thai restaurants in Abuja, as part of activities showcasing the country’s culture and heritage.
